question: An engineer must implement a VXLAN-based data center interconnect. The long-distance transport provided by a service provider is IP-based, supports a maximum MTU of 1554 bytes, and does not support outbound traffic replication. Which action must be taken to build the data center interconnect?
options: Create an IP access list and associate it with VNI to replicate traffic to remote VTEPs.
Configure a route map to associate the IPs of the remote VTEPs.
theory: When a VXLAN-based DCI transport is IP-based but cannot support multicast replication for BUM traffic, the fabric needs a unicast-based way to replicate that traffic and learn remote host reachability — this is exactly what BGP EVPN provides. With BGP EVPN as the control plane, VTEPs learn remote MAC/IP reachability via BGP updates (instead of data-plane flood-and-learn) and use ingress (head-end) unicast replication for BUM traffic, eliminating the dependency on multicast in the long-distance transport. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 3 — VXLAN MP-BGP EVPN Control Plane)
